exam.title: NiCat E-Commerce Pilot — 20 Marks
exam.instructions: Independent practice based on archived MMU course topics, not an official examination paper. Answer all 12 questions. MCQs earn 1 mark each; written answers are reviewed by staff.

options: A customer purchases goods through an online store
A lecturer gives an in-person lesson without digital systems
A shop counts stock only on paper
An employee attends an offline meeting
questions.explanation: E-commerce includes electronically mediated transactions in products or services.

questions.prompt: What is a business process in an organization?
options: A single computer hardware component
A coordinated sequence of activities that accomplishes a business task
The name of a web hosting provider
An encryption key for payment processing
questions.explanation: Business processes are coordinated activities, often across functions, that produce outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which system primarily records routine sales orders and shipping transactions?
options: Transaction processing system
Computer graphics renderer
Source code formatter
Network packet sniffer
questions.explanation: TPS handles routine operational transactions such as order entry and shipping.

questions.prompt: What is a primary purpose of business intelligence tools?
options: To replace customer service with manual paperwork
To analyze data to support decisions
To design only website color schemes
To block all external data
questions.explanation: Business intelligence organizes and analyzes data to improve business decisions.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a CRM system in a retail business?
options: To coordinate customer interactions and relationships
To compile a programming language
To configure a local network switch
To replace the accounting ledger with physical notes
questions.explanation: CRM organizes customer information and interactions to support sales, service, and retention.

questions.section: Abstract: Grupo Modelo: Competing on Processes
questions.prompt: What is a key benefit of an ERP system to a growing company?
options: It prevents every department from accessing shared records
It integrates information and processes across business functions
It only edits promotional images
It removes the need to define workflows
questions.explanation: ERP integrates business functions and related data, supporting coordinated processes.

questions.prompt: In Porter’s five-forces model, which force refers to competition among established firms in an industry?
options: Bargaining power of buyers
Threat of new entrants
Rivalry among existing competitors
Bargaining power of suppliers
questions.explanation: Industry rivalry assesses competition between existing firms.

questions.prompt: Why should managers consider organizational culture when implementing new e-commerce systems?
options: Culture influences adoption and resistance to new work practices
Culture determines the server clock speed
Culture replaces the need for process training
Culture guarantees every software rollout will succeed
questions.explanation: Shared norms, expectations, and routines can either support or resist systems changes.

questions.section: Managing Data in a Traditional File Environment
questions.prompt: What problem can arise when separate departments maintain inconsistent copies of customer records?
options: Guaranteed perfect data synchronization
Data redundancy and conflicting values
Automatic restoration of deleted records
Elimination of all security risks
questions.explanation: Duplicate independent files can cause redundancy and inconsistencies.

questions.prompt: Which practice most directly protects online shoppers when submitting payment information?
options: Using encrypted HTTPS connections
Displaying customers’ passwords on invoices
Sharing credentials among employees
Disabling all server access logs
questions.explanation: HTTPS protects data in transit between the user and the service, though other security controls are also needed.

questions.prompt: A Kenyan SME wants to launch an online store and strengthen customer retention. Discuss five ways customer information systems and a CRM could improve its operations or customer experience. (5 marks)
questions.explanation: Good answers link organized customer data to service, communication, loyalty, and business decisions, while respecting customer privacy.

rubric.description: Describes keeping a consistent record of customer information or interactions.
Describes improving customer service through case or enquiry history.
Describes targeted, consent-aware communication or offers.
Describes supporting repeat sales or customer retention.
Describes using customer insights to improve products or decisions.

questions.section: Two-way relationship between organizations and e-commerce MIS
questions.prompt: A college plans to replace manual registration and fee-tracking processes with a shared online system. Explain five organizational or operational considerations that management should address for a successful rollout. (5 marks)
questions.explanation: A successful transition considers people, organizational processes, data governance, secure access, and continuity alongside the technology.

rubric.description: Identifies staff training and support needs.
Identifies changes to existing procedures and departmental workflows.
Discusses access permissions or protection of student information.
Discusses managing resistance and communicating changes.
Discusses data quality, migration, availability, or continuity.
